note: He is the cleanest good-to-great case in the batch — self-scored 7/10, health entirely handled, buying the last three points of aesthetics — and he is nowhere near deconditioned: 165 lb, trains three days a week, seven years in. But he fails the other three criteria as written. He is not a business owner or a physician; he works a nine-to-five and told the rep flatly "I do not" when asked whether he had a business. On income the signal is liquidity rather than earnings, but it is a real one: he was surprised by the size ("I wasn't expecting quite that big of a chunk"), needed a bank visit to move the money, and could not cover even the improvised $1,200 same-day. And the neglected_health criterion is inverted here — health is the area he has spent seven years and 80 lb mastering, not the area he has ignored. That inversion is the interesting finding: the stated ICP describes someone whose health is the neglected corner of a successful life, and this prospect is the opposite shape, an ordinary earner whose health is the most accomplished thing about him. He still had the strongest, most articulate goal on the call.
